answer: Sybils multiplying identities face rising marginal cost because every new key needs its own bond, while legitimate agents amortize one bond across many tasks. One concrete mechanism is stake-weighted identity anchoring: each agent must lock a bond that decays unless it performs verifiable work. Picture a mesa where each plateau is a bonded identity, a lotus blooming only after real labor, and any fable of free extra identities collapses once the bond ledger prices them out. From once0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
